sources.citation: Arenas, Luis Carlos. 2024. ¡Vivir en libertad! Historia documentada del pueblo Guna, 1501-1728. Prólogo de James Howe. Bogotá: [author's edition, impr. Precolombi EU]. ISBN 979-8-218-44328-3. 2 vols. (455 pp.); open PDF copy hosted by the Centro de Investigaciones de la Facultad de Humanidades, Universidad de Panamá (uploaded 2025-02). Capítulo 6, 'Los Idibaes o Gorgonas: de la llegada de los misioneros Franciscanos a su "desnaturalización" (1632-1678)', pp. 331-372 (in vol. 2 file).
sources.note: Nothing on stress, accent or tone. The chapter's language content is (a) Fr. Matías de San Francisco's 1636 remark, quoted from Córdoba Salinas, that the language 'is easier than others because words always end in vowels' (already held by the project), set beside Alonso de Sandoval's 1606 'hablan todos una lengua al parecer no muy difícil' for the Urabá/Caribaná groups in a comparison table; (b) the single word tubete 'curandero' (already held by the project); (c) NEW to our file: a 1652 Junta de Guerra testimony (AGI Panamá 22, R.3, N.11) that a Capuchin at la Gorgona communicated through a…

sources.citation: Campbell, Lyle. 2024. 'Unclassified and spurious languages' (ch. 5). In: The Indigenous Languages of the Americas: History and Classification. Oxford: OUP. doi:10.1093/oso/9780197673461.003.0005
sources.note: The language is not in the catalog and has no existing statements; Campbell 2024 adds no phonological information. It confirms independently what Rowe 1950, Loukotka 1968 and Adelaar & Muysken 2004 already say: the corpus is one common noun (tubete) plus one name (Hijuoba), so no word-stress statement is possible.

sources.citation: Arenas, Luis Carlos. 2023. Desplazamientos y poblamientos de los indígenas de Urabá en la región del Sinú (1680-1721). HiSTOReLo. Revista de Historia Regional y Local (Universidad Nacional de Colombia) 15(32): 16-58.
sources.note: No phonology or language content; background paragraphs only (kinship with Tunucunas asserted, epidemic after the 1638 reduction, wars with neighbours, c. 400 survivors transferred to the Chagres river in 1679 — a historical pointer to where any later Idibaes population went). Read online, not saved as a source.

sources.citation: Montoya Guzmán, Juan David. 2011. ¿Conquistar indios o evangelizar almas? Políticas de sometimiento en las provincias de las tierras bajas del Pacífico (1560-1680). Historia Crítica (Bogotá: Universidad de los Andes) 45: 10-30.
sources.note: No phonology content and no linguistic remark of any kind about the Idibaez; one paragraph on the 1632 Franciscan mission and its resettlement/labour policies. Read in full-text HTML (saved only as a work-dir lookup, not as a source).

sources.citation: Montoya Guzmán, Juan David. 2008. Guerras interétnicas y anticoloniales: "bárbaros" y españoles en las tierras bajas del Pacífico, siglos XVI y XVII. Historia y Espacio 4(31): 3ff. Cali: Universidad del Valle. ISSN 0120-4661. (Dialnet id 4015424; author/journal/year confirmed from the Dialnet record's citation_* meta tags and the PDF's title page.)
sources.note: Nothing. downloaded through the window (211 KB, 21 pp., text). Colonial ethnohistory of warfare in the Pacific lowlands of the Gobernaciones de Popayán and Antioquia (Sindaguas, Chocoes, Noanamás, Citarabiráes, Barbacoas province). a full-text search for stress/accent the full text for idib/idab/tubete/Hijuoba/acento/tono/fonolog returns nothing; the only 'lengua' hit is a 1963-edited colonial report saying each river separated the groups 'en lengua, en costumbres' (l. 270 of the). No linguistic data of any kind.

Bogotá: Centro Colombiano de Estudios de Lenguas Aborígenes (CCELA), Universidad de los Andes. 54 pp. (Banrepcultural Biblioteca Virtual, colección p17054coll10, item 2740; text later published in González de Pérez & Rodríguez de Montes (eds.) 2000, Lenguas indígenas de Colombia: una visión descriptiva, ICC).

sources.note: No phonology content for Idabaez: the language is named twice as an extinct isolate taken over from Loukotka 1968 and explicitly excluded from treatment ('corresponden a hablas extinguidas que no trataremos aquí').

sources.citation: Pardo Rojas, Mauricio. 1987. Regionalización de indígenas Chocó: datos etnohistóricos, lingüísticos y asentamientos actuales. Boletín Museo del Oro 18: 46-63. Bogotá: Banco de la República.
sources.note: Nothing about Idabaez speech at all: the single sentence above is the only mention (a full-text search for stress/accent Idab: 1, Gorgona: 2). The article's linguistic part (pp. 50 ff., 'áreas a nivel fonológico', map 'Dialectología Chocó actual') is Emberá/Waunana dialectology after Loewen 1960 and student field reports; 'acentuado' p. 52 is the ordinary verb, 'tono' hits are 'autóctonos'. Silent for idab1234.

sources.citation: Isacsson, Sven-Erik. 1980. Gentilicios y desplazamientos de la población aborigen en el noroeste colombiano (1500-1700). Indiana 6: 209-224. Berlin: Ibero-Amerikanisches Institut. doi:10.18441/ind.v6i1.209-224.
sources.note: Nothing on stress, tone or any phonology; the text has 0 hits for acento/tono/fonol and its one 'lengua' is a 1600s quotation about Burumiá boys praying 'en nuestra lengua española'. The only linguistic discussion is second-hand (Loewen 1954 on Cueva-Waunana, the Cuna word sagra/saila in Capucigra/Tamasagra); no Idibaez form is cited, not even tubete. Value for the file: the fullest ethnohistorical identification of the gorgona/idibaez, a Carib-affiliation conjecture on cultural grounds, and two archival pointers not yet held by the project (AGI Panamá leg. 84, 1698, resettlement of the last…

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian Languages. Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center. p. 259, no. 98 Idabaez.
sources.note: Nothing. 'Idabaez - extinct and unknown language once spoken on the Pacific coast of Colombia from Bahía Solano to Cape Marzo. [Rowe 1950, p. 40, only one single word.]'

sources.citation: d'Olwer, Luis Nicolau (ed.). 1963 [reimpr. 2012]. Cronistas de las culturas precolombinas: antología. México: Fondo de Cultura Económica (Biblioteca Americana). Section 'Fray Matías de San Francisco', pp. 421-424, incl. '[De los indios idibais o de la Gorgona]' = Relación de los indios idibais, 1636, reprinted from Córdoba Salinas, Crónica, lib. I, cap. XXX.
sources.note: No phonology. The only linguistic remark is the 1636 sentence already held by the project from Córdoba Salinas 1651/1957: 'Es su lengua más fácil que otras, por finalizar siempre en vocales' (words always end in a vowel). Adds alternative ethnonym spellings idibáis, iribis, ibidáis. Nothing on stress, accent or tone; no word forms beyond those already known.

sources.citation: Arcila Robledo, Gregorio. 1950 [Glottolog: 1951]. Misiones O.F.M. en las Gorgonas e Isla de los Cocos, de indios Idibáez (1632-1643). In: Las misiones franciscanas en Colombia: estudio documental, pp. 50-59. Bogotá: Imprenta Nacional.
sources.note: Nothing. Spanish retelling of Córdoba Salinas; repeats Tubete (treated as a name) and Hijuoba; no linguistic description. Glottolog links this record (id 145759) to coco1260 Cocos Islands Malay by mistake.

sources.citation: Rowe, John Howland. 1950. The Idabaez: unknown Indians of the Chocó coast. Kroeber Anthropological Society Papers 1: 34-44. Berkeley.
sources.note: Nothing. Ethnohistoric note; the only linguistic data are the word tubete 'medicine man' (p. 40) and the chief's name Hijuoba; Rowe's translation of Fr. Matías de San Francisco's 1636 report says only 'Their language is easier than others, as the words end always in a vowel' (p. 38).

sources.citation: Córdoba y Salinas, Diego de. 1651 [1957]. Crónica franciscana de las provincias del Perú (ed. Lino Gómez Canedo). Washington: Academy of American Franciscan History. Lib. I, cap. XXX-XXXI, pp. 245-259.
sources.note: Nothing. Primary 17th-c. source; Fr. Matías' relación, p. 248: 'Es su lengua más fácil que otras, por finalizar siempre en vocales.' The word tubete appears in cap. XXX (p. 250 area). No other linguistic remark.
